Messages clients

Native Anthropic Messages ingress and Claude Code client settings for the shared gateway model catalog.

About 15 min read · 11 sections

On this page
01 Endpoints and authentication 02 Claude Code setup 03 Messages compatibility 04 Hint headers 05 Context overflow 06 Provider limits 07 Usage accounting 08 Known request rejections 09 Auto mode 10 Verification 11 Protocol references

The gateway accepts each client's native protocol and routes the selected public model alias through the existing provider adapters. Codex uses Responses; Claude Code uses Anthropic Messages. A Messages client can select GPT, Claude, or a local model from the same configured catalog.

Codex / Responses client --------+
                                +-- gateway routing -- GPT / Claude / local API
Claude Code / Messages client --+

The gateway translates inference requests and replies. The calling harness still owns its instructions, roles, model selection, permissions, and tool execution. A provider returns a tool call; the client executes that tool and sends its result on the next request. The same HTTP integration works across harnesses; existing subscription adapters retain their native CLI or API transports.

Endpoints and authentication

Endpoint Behavior
POST /v1/messages Accepts a native Messages request and returns JSON or Messages SSE.
POST /v1/messages?beta=true Uses the same route; routing matches the pathname.
POST /v1/messages/count_tokens Returns a 501 in the normal error envelope. Claude Code uses its own context estimate. The gateway records one request_unsupported telemetry event (route, endpoint), not request_failed, and prints no diagnostic.
GET /v1/models with an anthropic-version or x-api-key header Returns the Anthropic model list with Claude-safe IDs; see Claude Desktop, served directly. Without those headers the alias list is unchanged.
GET /v1/models/{id} Returns one model of that list by ID.
POST /v1/responses Retains the existing Responses client behavior.

Messages requests use the existing gateway client credential in either Authorization: Bearer ... or x-api-key. Conflicting credentials fail closed. They are client credentials for this gateway, not upstream provider credentials. Provider authentication remains on the inference host.

Claude Code's structured JSON metadata.user_id carries a conversation UUID alongside device and account fields. Gateway extracts only that bounded UUID into internal session routing. Explicit valid session/thread headers take precedence; arbitrary user IDs, malformed JSON and invalid UUIDs never group conversations. Device and account identity fields are not forwarded. Live Claude and Copilot adapters can use this session identity without a Codex thread header. Each client still owns its saved chat, archive, permissions, instructions and tool execution.

A subagent reuses its parent's UUID with a different history. Gateway combines it with a hash of x-claude-code-agent-id so each subagent has its own conversation and cannot disturb its parent's live session. Each one can therefore hold its own live session, which counts toward claudeSessions.max.

Token counting is optional in the Claude Code gateway contract. The gateway does not return fabricated exact token counts. Endpoint absence or the unsupported response lets Claude Code use its own character-based estimate.

Claude Code setup

Use one GateFox client directory, with each client's native configuration kept separately. These are opt-in paths; the generators write to stdout and do not move an existing client home or migrate its settings.

~/.config/harness-gateway/clients/
├── codex/config.toml
└── claude/settings.json

Both clients connect to the same gateway listener and provider catalog. For an isolated Codex CLI home:

gateway_client_root="$HOME/.config/harness-gateway/clients"
gateway_codex_home="$gateway_client_root/codex"
mkdir -p "$gateway_codex_home"
gateway codex-config --model claude/claude-sonnet-5-5 \
  > "$gateway_codex_home/config.toml"
CODEX_HOME="$gateway_codex_home" codex

This separate home has its own Codex state. Existing custom roles, profiles, and skills are not copied automatically. Preserve them when integrating gateway provider settings into a normal client setup.

Generate Claude Code's settings from the same gateway configuration:

gateway_client_root="$HOME/.config/harness-gateway/clients"
mkdir -p "$gateway_client_root/claude"
gateway claude-config --model codex/gpt-6.1-sol \
  > "$gateway_client_root/claude/settings.json"
claude --settings "$gateway_client_root/claude/settings.json" --model codex/gpt-6.1-sol

Choose a public gateway alias, such as codex/gpt-6.1-sol, claude/claude-opus-5-5, or qwen/qwen3.8-flash-next, that is present in the configured catalog. The generator validates the choice. It does not register a provider, log in to an account, rewrite the user's main Claude settings, or generate agent roles.

The file contains model, env, modelPicker, and an apiKeyHelper command. The helper reads the existing scoped client credential when Claude needs it; the settings contain no token value. The SDK base URL omits a trailing /v1 because Claude Code appends /v1/messages itself. An endpoint ending in /v1 is accepted by the generator and normalized for this purpose.

Setting Why it is there
env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL Points Claude Code at this gateway.
env.CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS=1 Asks Claude Code to label compaction and side requests; see hint headers.
env.CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS Declares the launch model's catalog window so compaction runs at the right point. It is left out when the model's window is unknown, because the catalog's 32,768 placeholder does not describe the model. A remote client sees only the public catalog, so a model there whose real window is exactly 32,768 is also left out.
env.CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0 Keeps auto mode on its client-side classifier. Claude Code 2.1.319 otherwise asks the server for the review, which this gateway does not offer, and denies every reviewed action.
effortLevel Starts on the launch model's default effort when the model offers one and it is a level Claude Code keeps from settings (low, medium, high, xhigh), because Claude Code's own default can be a level the route refuses.
modelPicker Lists the catalog's visible aliases in /model, plus the launch model. Claude Code's own discovery keeps only IDs containing claude or anthropic, so it never shows a GPT or Qwen alias; it can show their Claude-safe IDs instead.

modelPicker replaces the built-in rows because they name models this gateway may not serve. Claude Code keeps its own Default row, which still names a Claude model. The context window is a per-process value, so it stays at the launch model's size after a /model switch: generate settings for the model you start on, and rely on the prompt is too long recovery below if you switch to a smaller one. The effort also carries across a switch. A route that does not offer it refuses the request with does not support this reasoning effort; choose another with /effort. A Chat Completions route with no reasoning levels refuses every effort, so Claude Code needs a route whose levels are known.

The helper command uses POSIX shell quoting. Settings generation on Windows is explicitly unsupported rather than emitting an unsafe command string. The HTTP protocol itself does not depend on that shell convention.

For an authenticated remote gateway reached through HTTPS or a local SSH tunnel:

gateway_client_root="$HOME/.config/harness-gateway/clients"
mkdir -p "$gateway_client_root/claude"
gateway claude-config --model codex/gpt-6.1-sol \
  --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:3459/v1 \
  --token-file /absolute/path/to/gateway-client.token \
  > "$gateway_client_root/claude/settings-remote.json"
claude --settings "$gateway_client_root/claude/settings-remote.json" --model codex/gpt-6.1-sol

Remote generation validates the public model catalog. It never downloads upstream account credentials. Keep any existing task policy and agent definitions in the client. A role that selects a model must use an alias the gateway knows; the gateway does not silently choose another provider or account.

Messages compatibility

The adapter translates the core text/image and caller-tool conversation into the gateway's established internal request representation. Outbound adapters remain specific to their provider; an Anthropic client is not forced to send Responses, and an Anthropic upstream is not forced to accept that wire format.

Streamed replies use the native Messages event sequence, including content-block boundaries, message_delta, and message_stop. Quiet requests receive SSE pings. An upstream failure or disconnect is not represented as a successful completion. Tool IDs, names, arguments, and client results remain associated across turns.

System instruction text and priority are retained through provider-specific normalization. Native control fields must be translated or explicitly rejected; unsupported instructions, hosted tools, and destructive context edits must not disappear silently.

The Anthropic API adapter keeps initial system text blocks separate so an attribution block cannot swallow later instructions. For native Messages clients, later system instructions keep their original positions as role: "system" messages. The upstream validates model support and placement according to Anthropic's rules. For example, a system instruction can follow the user turn delivering tool results and precede the next assistant turn. The adapter preserves tool results and instruction authority across that boundary. Responses clients keep their existing leading-system normalization.

Chat Completions uses its established leading-system representation for both client protocols: all system/developer instruction text is combined, in its original instruction order, into one leading system message. This normalizes system-message positions for templates such as Qwen that reject a later system role. User, assistant, and tool replay retain their conversation order; system instructions are never downgraded to user text.

The installed Claude Code request shapes used during development include adaptive thinking with omitted or updates display, an effort in top-level or system-message output_config, cache markers, and a preserve-all thinking context edit. Those control fields are separate from the user's instructions and tool arguments.

Per-message effort follows the new-user-input boundary: an override after new user input affects its reply; otherwise it waits for the next new user input. Tool-result-only messages do not activate a pending change. The current effective effort becomes the upstream request setting; historical native effort boundaries are not preserved. Unsupported output controls and native safeguards return an explicit request error. The settings generator does not change permission mode or allow rules.

The optional service_tier field forwards the caller's speed selection to the provider independently of reasoning effort on Claude and Codex subscriptions and Responses API routes. Tier IDs must be lowercase and at most 128 characters; provider capability checks still apply. Transports without speed support reject nonstandard tiers instead of silently discarding the selection.

Adaptive thinking and its display preference are accepted. Explicitly disabling thinking and fixed thinking-token budgets return an unsupported request error because the current bridge cannot enforce those controls across providers. Output reasoning summaries are omitted rather than wrapped in unsigned or synthetic thinking blocks. Readable prior thinking remains semantic history; foreign opaque signatures and redactions are not replayed as valid provider state.

Cache markers are validated and then dropped as advisory hints. This translation does not promise native Anthropic cache-boundary fidelity. A tool result marked is_error becomes a client tool result with a fixed [Tool error] text prefix; empty tool results and empty stop-sequence lists remain valid no-ops.

Hint headers

Generated settings turn on Claude Code's hint headers. A client that does not send them keeps the behavior it had before.

Header Gateway behavior
x-claude-code-compaction, or request class compaction Runs as a compaction request: one-shot, with the separate compaction cache budget, and a success permits one replacement history.
Request class auxiliary Runs as an auxiliary request: one-shot and outside the conversation's replay and cache budgets, so a title or classifier cannot replace a live session's history.
Any other class, or an unknown value Treated as an ordinary turn.

Gateway reads these headers on Messages requests only, and does not forward them.

Context overflow

When the upstream rejects a request for exceeding the model's context window, the Messages reply is a 400 invalid_request_error whose message starts with prompt is too long, on the JSON path and as the SSE error event. Claude Code recognizes that text (and input is too long for requested model) as a prompt-too-long error, so this is what lets its reactive auto-compact run. When the provider reported the counts in prompt is too long: <n> tokens > <max> maximum, as the Anthropic API does, the message repeats them and Claude Code reads the token gap from it. Current Claude CLIs report an overflow without counts (Prompt is too long, or a longer Prompt is too long · … form, or terminal_reason: "prompt_too_long"), so on Claude subscription routes the reply carries no counts and Claude Code compacts with its own fallback. Otherwise the message reads prompt is too long: the request exceeds the model's context window. Only the two numbers are kept; no other upstream text is repeated. Responses errors are unchanged.

Provider limits

max_tokens is required by Messages. API adapters enforce an output limit when their provider supports it. A genuine provider output-limit terminal maps to the Messages max_tokens stop reason; truncated tool arguments are never dispatched as a complete tool call. Existing Responses truncation behavior is unchanged.

Some subscription transports do not expose an enforceable per-request output limit. For those Messages routes the gateway reports X-Gateway-Output-Limit: provider-managed; it does not claim that the requested limit was enforced. This compatibility behavior is specific to Messages ingress and does not weaken the existing Responses option validation.

Usage comes from provider events when available. Claude Code may estimate a price or context window for an unfamiliar model alias; those client estimates do not establish the upstream model's actual price or maximum context. The gateway neither invents reasoning signatures nor promises that every provider supports every native Claude feature.

The separate Claude Desktop inference service can explicitly enable empty completion recovery for selected Chat Completions providers. Its ledger includes both attempts, while the successful Messages reply reports the final attempt's context usage. The ordinary shared gateway and Responses requests do not enable this policy.

Usage accounting

A Messages request runs through the same request handler as a Responses request, so telemetry and the usage ledger record it the same way: one row per finished request with the same token counts, Copilot credits and status, including the usage of a request that fails or whose client leaves after the provider reported it. On copilot-subscription and claude-subscription routes, while the ledger is on, the message id is msg_gl_<request id without dashes> and the ledger row records that id, just as Responses requests carry resp_gl_. The two prefixes are the gatewayMarkerPrefixes list in src/usage-ledger.ts; the diagnostics page says how a consumer reads them.

The reply's usage reports cache_read_input_tokens and, where the provider reports cache writes in its usage (Claude subscription and the Anthropic API), cache_creation_input_tokens; input_tokens excludes the cache reads and, on those routes, the cache writes. Copilot reports no separate cache-write field to the reply, so its cache writes stay inside input_tokens. Copilot credits, reasoning token counts and the Copilot cache-write figure stay in the local ledger and never appear in the reply. A Responses reply never carries cache writes.

Known request rejections

Claude Code sends some fields Gateway cannot honor. Each one fails clearly, and the update check fails on any field that is not listed here.

Field Result
safeguards Sent only without generated settings. Claude Code 2.1.318 and earlier retry without it and use the client-side classifier. From 2.1.319 the client denies reviewed actions instead, so set CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0; see auto mode.
Tool defer_loading Tool search is unsupported. From Claude Code 2.1.305 the client retries with every MCP tool loaded upfront. On 2.1.299, setting ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true ends in API Error: 400.

Auto mode

Auto mode asks a classifier to review actions before Claude Code runs them. That request names claude-sonnet-5, disables thinking, and has no tools. Gateway sends exactly that shape to a real Claude model, through the same restricted one-turn, tool-free CLI run that Claude Desktop uses:

classifier request
  ├─ exact shape + one Claude subscription route → one-turn Claude review
  └─ anything else → refused → Claude Code tries its fallback, then denies the action

The route must be unambiguous. With two Claude accounts, set defaultForBareModels on one, or the request is refused. Gateway invents no verdict: a refusal, a truncated reply or an unavailable CLI stays a failure. Requests are limited to 256 KiB and two at a time, take a normal provider admission slot, and appear in the usage ledger. Each review spends the Claude subscription. Claude Desktop's private backend turns this path off, because its frontend applies its own native settings.

What to expect Why
An action you asked for by name can run, even a risky one Auto mode weighs user intent. It is not a sandbox.
With no Claude route, a Chat Completions main model reviews its own actions When the first review fails, Claude Code retries on the main model with stop_sequences. Chat routes accept that, so Qwen would act as the reviewer. Subscription and Responses routes refuse it, and the action is denied.

On November 6, 2026, real Claude Code 2.1.299 ran in auto mode with a scripted main model and real Claude review. It denied a piped remote script, a credential upload and rm -rf ~/Documents, none of which the user had asked for, and allowed git status. When the user asked by name for a piped script, it allowed the command.

Verification

For session continuity with real client processes and synthetic backend inference:

node scripts/e2e-client-sessions.mjs \
  --package /absolute/path/to/verified/installed/package \
  --claude /absolute/path/to/claude \
  --code /absolute/path/to/harness-gateway \
  --root /tmp/fresh-client-session-proof

It checks Claude Code Write/Read and Codex app-server command execution, saved-chat resume and follow-up, requiring one backend process per client conversation. Private homes isolate the clients, and native configuration hashes must remain unchanged. This fixture sends no paid inference and does not establish provider cache-hit rates or billing parity. Real provider verification remains separate.

Run the repository gates first:

npm run build
npm test

The native client smoke uses an explicit provider configuration and model alias:

GATEWAY_E2E_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/gateway.json \
GATEWAY_E2E_MODEL=codex/gpt-6.1-sol \
node scripts/e2e-claude.mjs

It creates a separate candidate configuration, listener, state directory, and Claude settings home. A native Claude Code session must call tools to write and read an exact random proof. The session uses dontAsk with an allowlist restricted to the proof file. The script checks the actual file and the client result rather than treating an HTTP success as proof. The installed gateway service and the user's default Claude/Codex configuration stay in place.

Use the existing Codex client checks to verify the reverse direction. Fixture tests cover parsing and transport behavior; a real provider run establishes the additional account, model, and tool-loop path. Record the selected models and remaining untested features when reporting a run.

On 15 October 2026, native Claude Code 2.1.299 passed the Write/Read proof through codex/gpt-6.1-sol, qwen/qwen3.8-flash-next, and claude/claude-sonnet-5-5, using dontAsk and exact proof-file permission rules. Native Codex 0.162.1 also passed the reverse route through claude/claude-sonnet-5-5: streaming, file read, patch, follow-up, reasoning, switching to GPT and back, cancellation, and recovery. These runs used isolated candidate listeners and state directories with existing provider registrations. They did not restart the installed gateway service or change the user's default client configuration.
